approved_classes.ex:AminoAcid: Amino acid, any of a group of organic molecules that contains a basic amino group (−NH2), an acidic carboxyl group (−COOH), and an organic R group (or side chain) that's unique to every amino acid.
approved_classes.ex:EssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids that are not produced by the body and must be obtained through food. They're also known as essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:SemiEssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids generated in the body, but production is insufficient; these amino acids are referred to as semi-essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:NonEssentialAminoAcid: Amino acids that are generated in the body and do not require supplementation; these amino acids are referred to as non-essential amino acids.
approved_classes.ex:AliphaticAminoAcid: A class representing amino acids with aliphatic side chains. Includes glycine, alanine, valine, leucine, and isoleucine.
approved_classes.ex:BranchedChainAminoAcid: A subclass of AliphaticAminoAcids that have branched aliphatic side chains (leucine, isoleucine, valine).
approved_classes.ex:HydroxylGroupContainingAminoAcid: A class representing amino acids with hydroxyl groups. Includes serine, threonine, and tyrosine.
approved_classes.ex:SulphurContainingAminoAcid: A class for amino acids containing sulfur (cysteine and methionine).
approved_classes.ex:AcidicAminoAcid: A class representing acidic amino acids, including aspartic acid and glutamic acid.
approved_classes.ex:BasicAminoAcid: A class for basic amino acids (lysine, arginine, histidine).
approved_classes.ex:AromaticAminoAcid: A class representing aromatic amino acids. Includes phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan.
approved_classes.ex:IminoAminoAcid: A class for the unique amino acid proline, which has an imino group instead of a primary amine (-NH2).
approved_classes.ex:HeterocyclicAminoAcid: A class representing heterocyclic amino acids (histidine, tryptophan, and proline).

ex:isMadeUpOf.comment: Protein is made up of amino acids, which are the building blocks of the molecule.

ex:hasFunctionalGroup.comment: The amino ( -NH2) group is basic, whereas the carboxyl ( -COOH) group is acidic.

ex:hasRGroup.comment: The remaining two bonds of the α-carbon atom are generally satisfied by a hydrogen (H) atom and the R group [1–6, 9].

ex:isSolubleIn.comment: Most of the amino acids are usually soluble in water and insoluble in organic solvents.

ex:meltsAt.comment: Amino acids are generally melted at a higher temperature often above 2000 C.

ex:tastes.comment: Taste: Amino acids are also sweet (Glycine, Alanine and Valine), tasteless (Leucine) or Bitter (Arginine & Isoleucine).

ex:hasOpticalIsomer.comment: All amino acids except glycine possess optical isomers because of the presence of asymmetric α-carbon atoms and show optical activity.

ex:hasZwitterion.comment: The name zwitter is derived from the German word which implies hybrid. Zwitter ion (or) dipolar ion is a hybrid molecule containing positive & negatively ionic groups.

ex:hasIsoelectricPoint.comment: The proton shifts from the carboxyl group to the amino group of the self-molecule at normal pH cellular levels.

ex:undergoesDecarboxylation.comment: The amino acids will undergo alpha Decarboxylation to make the corresponding amines. Histidine → Histamine + CO2 Tyrosine → Tyramine + CO2 Tryptophan → Tryptamine + CO2

ex:reactsWithAlkalies.comment: Amino acids react with alkalies to make Salts.

ex:reactsWithAlcohols.comment: Amino acids are reacted with an alcohol to form, Ester.

ex:reactsWithAmmonia.comment: The carboxyl group of dicarboxylic amino acids reacts with NH3 to form Amides. Aspartic acid + NH3→ Asparagine Glutamic acid + NH3→Glutamine

ex:reactsWithMineralAcids.comment: When the amino acids are treated with mineral acids (like HCl), it forms Acid Salts.

ex:hasNinhydrinReaction.comment: When Amino acids (or) Imino acid react with Ninhydrin molecule it gives Color. When it gives Purple color (Ruhemanns Complex) the Unknown sample is Amino acids (Which have primary amine NH2) or it gives Yellow color the Unknown sample is Imino acid (-NH-).

ex:isLOrD.comment: Only L-amino acids are manufactured in cells and incorporated into proteins. Some D -amino acids are found within the cell walls of bacteria, but not in bacterial proteins.

ex:isEssential.comment: These are amino acids that are not produced by the body and must be obtained through food. They're also known as essential amino acids.

ex:isSemiEssential.comment: Amino acids generated in the body, but production is insufficient; these amino acids are referred to as semi-essential amino acids.

ex:isNonEssential.comment: Amino acids that are generated in the body and do not require supplementation; these amino acids are referred to as non-essential amino acids.

ex:hasAliphaticSideChain.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid has an aliphatic side chain.

ex:hasBranchedChain.comment: Indicates if the amino acid is a branched-chain amino acid (BCAA).

ex:hasHydroxylGroup.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid has a hydroxyl group.

ex:containsSulphur.comment: Indicates if the amino acid contains sulfur (cysteine, methionine).

ex:isBasicAminoAcid.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is basic.

ex:hasAromaticRing.comment: Indicates if the amino acid has an aromatic ring (phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan).

ex:hasIminoGroup.comment: Indicates if the amino acid has an imino group (proline).

ex:isHeterocyclicAminoAcid.comment: Indicates whether the amino acid is heterocyclic.
